title: Scholarship and Recipe
premise: Jonah Quintana, a scholarship student at elite Meridian Prep, hides behind an anonymous coding forum account where he's brutally honest about the school's secrets — until his posts start predicting real events, including the disappearance of his best friend Theo, who leaves behind only a set of keys to a locked room beneath the library. Following the keys, Jonah uncovers a network of students trading favors and secrets, and realizes Theo vanished deliberately, leaving clues only Jonah can read. As prom approaches and the school closes in on his anonymous identity, Jonah must choose between exposing everything to save Theo's reputation or protecting the found family they built. In the end, he unmasks himself at prom, reveals the truth on his own terms, and reunites with Theo — choosing who he is when every label comes off.
about_author: Astrid Dunmore is the pen name of a former scholarship kid who spent four years watching private-school politics from the outside. She writes stories about clever, anxious teens who find their people in the unlikeliest corners.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Establishes his double life: quiet scholarship coder by day, sharp-tongued anonymous poster 'nullset' by night. He counts 94 days to graduation while navigating Meridian Prep's social hierarchy. Emotional beat: restless isolation, longing to be seen.

chapters.title: The Keys in the Locker
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Theo misses their weekly diner ritual, then vanishes entirely; school officials offer vague answers. Jonah finds a locker note containing a brass key etched with coordinates. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Nullset Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah and forum replies. His anonymous post about Theo goes viral within the school; someone replies 'you already know where to look.' Beat: the anonymity that protected him becomes a trap.

chapters.title: Under the Library
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The key opens a forgotten archive room full of old student files and a ledger of traded secrets. He finds Theo's handwriting: a list of names, Jonah's among them. Beat: vertigo — his best friend knew more than he let on.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Things
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The school's fixer and Theo's other close friend confronts Jonah, having noticed him snooping. Uneasy alliance forms over shared grief and mutual suspicion. Beat: reluctant connection, first crack in Jonah's armor.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Favors
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Decoding the ledger reveals generations of students trading silence for advantage — including a teacher and a trustee. Someone has been watching the room recently. Beat: stakes escalate from personal mystery to institutional rot.

chapters.title: Detention and Dinners
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Priya drags Jonah into her chaotic found-family dinner nights with outcast students Dez, Marisol, and Finn. Jonah resists, then softens. Beat: warmth he didn't ask for, guilt over keeping secrets from them.

chapters.title: Trace Route
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Using his skills, he traces forum activity and finds someone impersonating nullset, posting to flush him out. A near-miss with the dean. Beat: paranoia closing in, the net tightening.

chapters.title: What Theo Left Behind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She shares letters Theo sent her, revealing he was being blackmailed over a secret and planned his own exit. Jonah realizes Theo trusted them both with pieces, not wholes. Beat: heartbreak reframed as trust.

chapters.title: The Trustee's Son
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The trail leads to Cameron Voss, charming legacy kid whose family anchors the blackmail network. Cameron offers Jonah a deal: stay quiet, get a recommendation letter. Beat: temptation versus integrity.

chapters.title: Marisol's Map
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The group pools knowledge; Marisol recognizes locations in Theo's clues as spots tied to her older sister's era at Meridian. The network is older than anyone thought. Beat: collective purpose ignites.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Prom becomes the stage everyone's maneuvering around; Cameron angles to control it, the dean watches Jonah, and tickets require ID. Beat: comic relief laced with dread — the clock is literal now.

chapters.title: Finn's Confession
chapters.summary: Finn's POV. Finn admits he once sold a secret through the network to survive expulsion, and fears what exposure means for kids like them. Group fractures over whether to go public. Beat: moral complexity, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Burner Phones and Bad Ideas
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He contacts Theo's burner number; a reply arrives — not Theo, but someone using his phone. Jonah sets a trace and gets a location: a storage unit across town. Beat: hope and manipulation entwined.

chapters.title: The Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Jonah and Priya POV alternating. Inside: Theo's laptop, journals, and evidence he was assembling to expose the network before disappearing. They realize he's alive and hiding by choice. Beat: relief curdling into hurt — why leave us behind?

chapters.title: Reading Theo's Journals
chapters.summary: Theo's journal entries rendered as interludes, framed by Jonah's reactions. Reveals Theo's blackmail, his shame, and his plan to protect Jonah specifically. Beat: devastating tenderness; Jonah understands at last.

chapters.title: Cameron's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cameron threatens to expose Jonah's scholarship irregularities and nullset identity unless the evidence disappears. The dean summons him. Beat: darkest hour — duty, fear, and love pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Group POV round-robin. The found family votes on what to do: bury it, leak it, or Jonah goes public as nullset at prom. Finn flips, choosing courage. Beat: unity forged through disagreement.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days Later
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Prom night. Wearing the mask literally — a plain domino mask — Jonah takes the mic, unmasks himself, and tells the room everything, naming names but shielding the vulnerable. Beat: triumphant vulnerability.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Parking Lot
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Consequences land: investigations open, Cameron's family scrambles, the dean resigns quietly. Jonah waits by the diner like old times. Beat: exhale after the storm, changed friendships.

chapters.title: The Diner Booth
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Theo appears, thinner, wary, forgiven. They talk until the coffee goes cold; Theo explains, apologizes, and asks to come home. Beat: reconciliation without easy absolution.

chapters.title: Who I Am With the Labels Off
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, final week of school. Graduation, the archive room sealed, nullset retired with one last post signed with his real name. He chooses college nearby, keeps the family he found. Beat: quiet, earned hope — identity chosen, not assigned.
